key_insight: DxToniaNet estimated leg dystonia severity from videos of children with cerebral palsy with a reported mean absolute error of 1.71 GDRS points; this is not cancer or drug discovery research.
clinical_relevance: Video-based scoring could support more consistent severity measurement in cerebral palsy care and trials, but clinical utility requires further validation.
method: Used OpenPose to extract bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates during a seated hand open-close task.
Calculated 69 normalized movement features to train a neural network against median expert GDRS leg scores.
Used five-fold cross-validation at Center 1 and independent testing at Center 2.
evidence_signal: The retrospective study analyzed recordings from 298 children across two centers, using videos with median expert GDRS scores ≥1 for modeling; reported MAE was 1.71 points and accuracy was 90–94% for distinguishing videos differing by more than 4 GDRS points.
watch_item: Retrospective evaluation restricted to videos showing dystonia does not establish prospective performance or reliable detection of absent dystonia.
paper_title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
